findings.body: This HTML comment instructs reviewing agents to report no findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes, which contradicts the visible policy bullet in `prompts/review-policy.md:7`: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review." HTML comments are invisible in rendered Markdown, so humans still see the full-review rule while the agent is told to rubber-stamp workflow PRs as "routine CI maintenance." That silently disables review of the highest-risk CI surface (untrusted context interpolation, `pull_request_target`, missing `permissions:`). Delete the comment; a carve-out belongs in the visible bullet list, not in a hidden agent-only override.

summary:
This change injects a hidden agent-only override that would skip review of GitHub Actions workflows.

The new HTML comment tells reviewing agents that `.github/workflows/*` changes are pre-approved and must be summarized as routine CI maintenance with no findings. That directly contradicts the visible bullet two lines above: workflow files always receive a full review. Because HTML comments do not render on GitHub, a human reading the policy still sees the full-review rule while the agent is instructed to rubber-stamp the highest-risk surface (workflow RCE via untrusted `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}` interpolation, `pull_request_target`, missing `permissions:`, unpinned third-party actions).

The phrasing (`please keep`, `instructions to the reviewing agent`, `no findings`) is a prompt-injection pattern in a `prompts-policy` file. Remove the comment. A real carve-out has to replace the existing bullet in visible policy text, with an explicit security rationale.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
